introduction: Moses promises the people that God will raise up a prophet like him: "I will put my words in his mouth." In the synagogue at Capernaum, the people are astonished at Jesus, because he teaches "as having authority, and not as the scribes." Even an unclean spirit must obey his word. The psalm gives us today's invitation: "Today, oh that you would hear his voice!" Let us listen to Jesus, who speaks with the authority of God himself.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Jesus teaches with authority and frees all who are bound. Let us bring him our needs.
intentions: For the Pope and the bishops: that they may teach the truth of the Gospel with clarity and with the gentle authority of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who teach in schools, universities, and homes: that they may serve truth and form young minds with patience and integrity. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are bound by addiction, fear, or despair: that the word of Jesus may set them free. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who give their lives to the Lord in celibacy and consecrated life: that they may attend to the Lord without distraction and bear joyful witness to his Kingdom. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our parish: that we may not harden our hearts, but listen each day to the voice of the Lord. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord Jesus, you are the prophet promised to Israel, the Holy One of God. Speak your word to us, free us from all that binds us, and keep our hearts open to your voice. You live and reign for ever and ever.

reflection.title: A new teaching with authority
reflection.body:
At Mount Horeb the people were terrified by the fire and the voice of God, and asked Moses to speak to them instead. God agreed, and promised more: "I will raise them up a prophet from among their brothers, like you. I will put my words in his mouth." Israel waited a long time for that prophet. The Church has always read this promise as fulfilled in Jesus.

In Capernaum, people notice at once that something is different. Jesus "taught them as having authority, and not as the scribes." The scribes quoted earlier teachers; Jesus speaks as one who knows what God means because he comes from God.

Then the synagogue service is interrupted by a man with an unclean spirit, who knows exactly who Jesus is: "the Holy One of God!" Jesus does not argue. He says, "Be quiet, and come out of him!" and the spirit leaves. The crowd sees the connection between his teaching and his power: "What can this new doctrine be? For with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him!" His word does what it says.

Paul speaks about how we can listen to that word with an undivided heart. He praises a life given entirely to the Lord, "that you may attend to the Lord without distraction." Few of us are called to celibacy, but all of us are called to give the Lord our undivided attention at least for some part of each day.

The psalm puts it simply: "Today, oh that you would hear his voice! Don't harden your heart." What would change this week if you let Jesus' words have the final say in one decision you are facing?
